event: Nala calls "Hello?" toward the moving patch of grass, steady and loud.
The voice is the woman's voice again, still not what she expects to hear.
She straightens to her full height, which is not much, and sets her hands on her hips.
No answer comes in words; the sniffing stops, and the grass around it goes quiet.
A dry rattle comes from where the sniffing was, like glass beads shaken in a cup.
The blades part and she sees it: a low, broad body about knee-high, with grey-green hide.
It has a blunt snout, lifted and working, and a back bristling with pale glassy quills.
The quills look much like the grass blades themselves.
It does not come on; it holds a few body lengths off, quills raised and trembling.
It begins to circle her, slow and sidelong, from her left around toward her back.
Its snout stays turned on her the whole way.
The cut on her palm is still beading, and a drop runs down to her wrist.
Each time her hand moves, the snout dips after it.
When she turns her head to follow it, it stops and rattles again.
When she faces it square, it goes still and only watches.
Then it moves on again, patient, sliding out of the edge of her sight toward her back.
